encounters.cc: Six-month history of epigastric pain worsening with meals and 10-pound weight loss

lines: Six-month history of epigastric pain worsening with meals and 10-pound weight loss
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of epigastric pain that worsens with meals.
She also reports a 10-pound weight loss over the same period but denies nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits.
- Interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue disease
Her past medical history is significant for gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and a remote Helicobacter pylori infection treated 5 years ago.
She does not smoke or consume alcohol.
Physical examination reveals mild tenderness to palpation in the epigastric region without rebound or guarding.
Biopsy of the mass is performed, and histopathology is consistent with extranodal marginal zone B cell lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma).
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) reveals a 2 cm ulcerated mass in the gastric antrum.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of progressive skin tightening, difficulty swallowing, and dry cough

lines: Six-month history of progressive skin tightening, difficulty swallowing, and dry cough

A 53-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis, interstitial lung disease, and a history of gastric MALT lymphoma diagnosed in January 2020 presents to the rheumatology clinic with a 6-month history of increasing shortness of breath and a dry cough.
She also reports difficulty swallowing and a sensation of tightness in her skin, which has progressively thickened over her face, neck, and the upper part of her chest.
- Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) of the stomach (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue disease
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Librarian.
Taut, shiny skin with loss of normal facial creases and telangiectasias over her face and chest.
Her lung auscultation reveals bibasilar velcro-like crackles.
Her fingers show sclerodactyly and there are no digital ulcers.
- Diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO): 45% of predicted

encounters.cc: Six-month history of increasing difficulty climbing stairs and rising from seated position

lines: Six-month history of increasing difficulty climbing stairs and rising from seated position
The patient is a 54-year-old female with systemic sclerosis, scleroderma renal crisis, and gastric MALT lymphoma returning for follow-up.
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of increasing difficulty climbing stairs and getting up from a seated position.
She reports a mild, diffuse joint pain but denies skin rash or involvement of the distal muscles.
- Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) of the stomach (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue disease
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Librarian.
On physical examination, she has symmetrical proximal muscle weakness in her upper and lower extremities.
There is no muscle tenderness, and the rest of the examination is unremarkable.
A muscle biopsy is performed, which shows a mononuclear infiltrate surrounding necrotic and regenerating muscle fibers.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and nonproductive cough

lines: Six-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and nonproductive cough
With systemic sclerosis and polymyositis, the patient returns for follow-up.
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and a nonproductive cough.
She denies any fever, chest pain, or wheezing.
- Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) of the stomach (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue disease
She has a past medical history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and hypothyroidism.
She takes for which she takes omeprazole and levothyroxine, respectively.
She has never smoked and works as a librarian.
Oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.
On physical examination, fine inspiratory crackles are heard at the lung bases bilaterally.
Pulmonary function tests reveal a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 78% predicted, a total lung capacity (TLC) of 72% predicted, and a diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) of 65% predicted.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of severe headache, shortness of breath, and generalized malaise

lines: Two-day history of severe headache, shortness of breath, and generalized malaise

This 56-year-old female with systemic sclerosis, interstitial lung disease, polymyositis, and history of scleroderma renal crisis in 2021 presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of severe headache, shortness of breath, and generalized malaise.
She reports that her blood pressure has always been within the normal range during her routine visits.
- Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) of the stomach (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue disease
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Librarian.
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 190/110 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute.
She has diffuse skin thickening and telangiectasias on her face.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals fine crackles at the bases.
- Urinalysis: Proteinuria, hematuria, and red blood cell casts
